title: MCP Tasks Extension: Durable Work on a Stateless Core
service: DurableTask: an MCP Tasks extension server: server-directed task handles, tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel, a worker that runs task-backed tools, a store shared through a directory, a subscriptions/listen SSE stream, worker leases and expiry cleanup

parts.lesson_anchor: Poll with tasks/get (outer resultType complete, task state in status); Cancellation Is Cooperative; Durability, Expiry, and Ownership (ttlMs measured from creation, null for no limit); code/main.py TaskService.tasks_get, tasks_cancel and Task
planted_bugs: _fail_if_overdue compares the clock with expires_at() without handling None; the TypeError surfaces while polling a different task, inside the sweep that tasks_get runs over every task, when it reaches the task whose ttlMs is null
tasks_get sets the outer resultType from the task's status (task while running, complete once finished), the parser bug the lesson describes, written on the server
tasks_cancel's else branch cancels every task that is not working, so a completed task loses its result; the damage shows on the next tasks/get
Task.expires_at adds the ttl to last_updated_at although the docstring and the lesson measure it from createdAt
tasks_get fails overdue tasks by scanning the whole store before every poll, O(tasks) per tasks/get
parts.timing_assert: 3000 tasks in a MemoryStore, 20 polls with the clock advancing one second per poll, timed after gc.collect(), under 0.04 s. Measured here under load (load average 8 to 14): the whole-store sweep takes 0.58 to 0.96 s (at least 14x the limit), the per-task check 0.3 to 0.9 ms (at least 40x under it). A sweep throttled to once per clock second fails as well, because the clock advances between polls
parts.overfix_guard: dropping the expiry check to make polling fast fails 'a task expires ttlMs after it was created'; cancelling working tasks at once, as code/main.py does, fails the cooperative check, and making cancel a no-op leaves a task waiting for input uncancelled; a cancel that keeps a finished task's status but saves it again changes lastUpdatedAt; ttlMs null read as expired, an exclusive boundary and ttlMs read as seconds all fail; an expiry shown but not saved keeps the old lastUpdatedAt; tasks/cancel losing its expiry check altogether (instead of checking the one task) cancels an overdue task that should have failed

parts.lesson_anchor: Durability, Expiry, and Ownership (persist id, status, timestamps, ttl, poll interval, ownership, result or error, input requests and every issued key; atomic writes); Stateless Core, Stateful Application (a task id routes to any replica backed by the same durable store); code/main.py TaskStore.persist and reload

deviations: Part 1 runs on MemoryStore, the in-memory store that ships with the service, because the file store is what Part 2 builds and Part 1 must pass before Part 2 exists. The suggested fourth bug (TaskStore.get reloading the whole directory) and its guard (two TaskServices on one directory see each other's updates) therefore move into Part 2's requirements: get reads one file, timed over 2000 files, and two stores on one directory see each other's writes, in both directions, which also rules out the lesson's load-once cache and a read-through cache. Part 1's performance bug becomes the lazy-expiry sweep that tasks_get runs over every task, and a fifth bug is added: the comparison with expires_at() that crashes on a task whose ttlMs is null, which surfaces while polling a different task.

Part 1's outer resultType bug keeps the server-side form of the lesson's parser bug (task while running, complete once finished). The nested result's own resultType and serverInfo are checked in Part 3, where the worker stores the tool's CallToolResult, because Part 1 has no worker.

Cancellation is cooperative in a way the tests can see: a working task only records the request (cancel_requested) and its worker cancels it at the next step without running the tool, while a task waiting for input is cancelled at once. code/main.py cancels every non-terminal task immediately; the lesson allows either and asks clients not to infer a final state from the acknowledgement.

Part 2's 'ttlMs null versus missing' trap is the writer that drops null fields together with a reader that fills a missing ttl_ms with the default; every record written by the reference has every key. Part 2 also requires atomic replacement observably: a reader that opened the old file keeps reading the old record (POSIX only, since Windows will not rename over an open file).

Superseded keys: the worker runs only while nothing is outstanding, so a key is superseded when a newer request replaces the question (approve_outline after a decline, then approve_outline_2). The rule the service implements covers unknown, fulfilled and superseded keys at once: only outstanding keys are accepted. A tool that asks again for an issued key fails the task with -32603.

Part 4 polls the shared store on ticks supplied by the caller, so it also sees changes made by other instances; snapshots come from tasks/get itself, so lazy expiry and ownership are the same as polling. No initial snapshots are sent after the acknowledgement. The stream ends, when nothing is left to watch, with the listen request's result carrying subscriptionId next to serverInfo; that final result comes from lesson 09 (this phase), not from this lesson's text.

Part 5 replaces the nested-structure part, which this lesson does not have, with exercises 3 and 5 as the chapter plan suggests: leases are <taskId>.lease files next to the task files, created exclusively, expiring on the injected clock, with fencing before commit; the sweep fails an overdue task that is still running and deletes it on a later sweep, and deletes an overdue task that had already finished. A deleted task answers 'task not found', as quiz/quiz.md's answer to Q12 describes; the expiry error EXPIRED_ERROR (-32603, Task expired) is this service's choice, also following that answer, since the lesson names no code.

Out of scope, to stay clear of other lessons: A2A cards and artifacts (lesson 19), races between request cancellation and task cancellation, and two workers taking over one expired lease at the same moment (lesson 29), SSE event ids (lessons 09 and 29). The HTTP layer, Mcp-Name and server/discover are not part of this pack.
